messages:
Nina (PMM): Quick standup: we need a compact 'swap-sell' battlecard for SDRs to use when competing with cloud provider endpoints and single-tenant LLM APIs. Keep it < 120 chars per line.
Evan (Growth): Goal: reduce friction for SDRs to schedule demos. One-tap rebuttals + 2 micro-bench stats should do it.
Kira (SalesOps): Also add a triage matrix: tag leads by intent (latency, compliance, cost, scaling). Route high-intent to AE.
Diego (Product): Technical differentiators to call out, short form: "single API across deployment modes", "canary + A/B rollouts", "inference-level caching and batching".
Alex (Design): I'll make a vertical Slack card and a printable 1-pager. Visual hook: a tiny pipeline showing Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.
Nina (PMM): Draft one-liners for SDRs (not claims, just conversation starters):
- "We let you keep the same API as you upgrade infra — no rewrite."
- "We focus on predictable SLOs and graceful fallbacks so apps don't flake."
- "We tune inference (batching, cache, quantization) so cost falls as usage stabilizes."
Evan (Growth): Micro-bench stats (short):
- "Typical p95 drop: 20-40% after dedicated tuning (depends on seq len)."
- "Unit cost improvement: material via batching + prefix cache (customer-dependent)."
Diego (Product): Rephrase to avoid guarantees: "Customers often see p95 latency improvements after deploying to Dedicated and enabling batching/caching."
Kira (SalesOps): Objection flows we need (short bullets):
- Prospect: "We already use CloudCorp endpoints."
  - SDR: "Totally. Redwood can proxy or replace gradually — you get canary routing and automated fallback without ripping things out."
- Prospect: "Hosted API is simpler for us."
  - SDR: "Start hosted for speed, then move to dedicated/private without changing client code."
- Prospect: "We're worried about egress and compliance."
  - SDR: "We support VPC/private control planes, KMS integrations, and audit logs AE route."
Evan (Growth): Competitive soundbites vs vendor buckets (tweet-length):
- Big cloud infra: "They sell capacity; we ship inference ops. Serving primitives, routing, and SLOs included."
- LLM API vendors: "Great for fast POCs; harder to migrate. Redwood keeps dev ergonomics + mobility."
- Inference runtimes: "Libraries vs managed runtime + orchestration + observability  for production."
- Embedding specialists: "Embeddings are a slice; we manage full-gen + routing + fallbacks."
Alex (Design): Slack card mock (text-only):
```
Swap-sell kit: Redwood (30s)
 Same API across Hosted / Dedicated / Private
 Canary & fallback policies to avoid outages
 Cost levers: batching, prefix cache, quantization
Need demo? reply "demo" and we'll prioritize.
```
Diego (Product): Tiny demo snippet for 'show migration' (one request, same code):
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-4b", "prompt":"Hello" }'
```
Swap the model or endpoint behind the scenes, no client changes.
Nina (PMM): Routing rules (SalesOps): tag leads mentioning latency/SLA/private/compliance/cost as high-intent and route to Solutions. Kira: can you add lead mapping into Salesforce?
Kira (SalesOps): On it. Will add 4 custom lead reasons and automation rule.
WebinarBot: Reminder: webinar assets deadline in 4 business days. Calendar: https://cal.example/webinar/2291
Evan (Growth): Next steps: I'll write 2 SDR scripts (initial + rebuttal) and a 1-pager with micro-bench notes.
Alex (Design): I'll post Slack-card PNG and one-pager in #marketing-assets by EOD tomorrow.
Diego (Product): I'll hand over two one-line product blurbs and the demo snippet.
Nina (PMM): Great. We'll assemble into a single battlecard and run a 10-minute SDR playbook session before the webinar. :sparkles:
